Datacurve has raised a $15M Series A to provide frontier training data to the world’s leading foundation-model labs, helping to push the boundaries of what AI can do. Instead of traditional data labeling, Datacurve uses a “bounty system” where skilled engineers contribute to hard-to-source datasets and get paid — over $1M in bounties so far. But co-founder Serena Ge says the real advantage is treating contributors like users, not contractors, creating a platform people actually want to use. As AI models shift from simple datasets to complex RL environments, demand for high-quality post-training data is exploding. Datacurve believes its approach could extend beyond software engineering to fields like finance, marketing, and even medicine. Congrats on the round, Serena, Charley Lee , and team! https://lnkd.in/gPhQnh4a ...more ...more

Have you seen billion dollar AI company founders and top VC partners standing outside a door, all trying to figure out a digital lock? I have. Jokes aside, here's what I actually learned at Venture with Grace CEO Club Dinner No. 12. 1. Everyone has something to offer. Billion dollar founders are still human. They have families. They sleep. They eat food. Even in the AI era, what connects people isn't technology. It's time spent together. Empathy still wins. 2. Fully commit. Partners from top VC firms showed up early. Not on time. Early. If it's on your calendar, you show up. Doesn't matter if it's traffic, weather, or World Cup match 40 minutes away. 3. Be a problem solver. I overheard founders helping other founders. Execs breaking down hard concepts for people who needed it. Nobody was selling. Everyone was just... helping. The most successful people in the room were the ones giving something away. Here's the thing. We had founders in that room worth over $6.8B combined. We had partners who've backed some of the most important AI companies on earth. And the biggest takeaway wasn't about AI at all. It was human connection. Many thanks to our amazing partners Chargebee , Nebius , and Findem for making tonight possible. On to the next one. #AI #VentureCapital #Startups #SanFrancisco #worldcup

Opus 4.8 is now on DeepSWE. On the default high thinking effort, it scores 6% higher than Opus 4.7 xhigh, while also lowering average cost per task. 4.8 delivers efficiency gains by solving tasks in fewer steps, directly reducing the total number of input tokens required per task. Check out our full benchmark here: deepswe.datacurve.ai
First benchmark with many to come! Exciting times.

Introducing DeepSWE, a new long-horizon agentic coding benchmark. Frontier coding models look close in capability on many public benchmarks, but developers report that the differences feel much larger, especially around reasoning, planning, persistence, and execution over long horizons. DeepSWE solutions are ~5.5x longer than SWE-Bench Pro by lines of code, with 2x longer agent trajectories. Tasks are written from scratch, preventing any pre-training contamination risk. Blog: deepswe.datacurve.ai/blog Repo: https://lnkd.in/gNVKz5Qg Give your own models a spin and let us know what you think!
